MENTOR: You've done the pivot lesson, and this one builds on it.

In this lesson you'll move several layers as one group by attaching them to a single invisible handle.

Which layers should move as one, like the parts of a lower third or a logo lockup?

### Turn 2: the project is an open comp
LEARNER: Why do I need a null at all? What does a parent actually pass down to the layers under it?
MENTOR: A parent passes its position, scale and rotation down to every layer under it. If the parent slides, turns or grows, its children do too, and each child still plays its own animation on top. Hatch in this comp already works this way: it follows Hatch Rig. Two things don't pass down: opacity and effects. A parent's fade or blur never reaches its children. You use a null as the parent because a null never shows in the render, so it can't add its own look to the group. It's an invisible handle you put exactly where the group should turn or scale from.

Which layers in this comp should move as one?
